Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked great. Before we move to a formal PoC, procurement and our platform team asked for a clearer picture of economics. A few concrete items: 

- For a 3-month PoC (~150M tokens expected), can you confirm any promo/credit you can apply?
- If we convert to a committed monthly spend after the PoC, what do your per-token slab discounts look like (e.g., 0-100M / 100-500M / 500M+)?
- Any standard billing cadence for mid-market customers?

We also need a short SOW to share with legal. Can you send your PoC template and a simple pricing grid we can review with procurement?

Best,

BrightCart

Evelyn — great to hear you and your team found the demo useful. Looping in Rishi (sales lead) and Grace (solutions) to align on numbers and SOW.

Short answers up front:
- PoC credits: We can offer a $20,000 platform credit to apply against usage for a 3-month PoC once a mutually-signed SOW is in place.
- Commit/volume slabs (illustrative): 0–100M tokens: $0.0012/token; 100–500M: $0.0009/token; 500M+: $0.00065/token.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoice with 30-day payment terms (standard), with the option for net-45 on approved PO.

I'll attach a draft PoC SOW and our current pricing grid for procurement. If BrightCart can commit to a 6‑month reserved baseline after the PoC, we can increase credit to $30k and apply an extra 5% off listed slab prices for the first quarter after conversion.

Attaching: BrightCart_PoC_SOW.pdf, redwood_pricing_grid_v2.xlsx

Thanks,

Following up on the numbers — quick clarifications from our side that often come up with procurement: 

1) How are tokens measured for discounts? We price on total monthly token usage across generation + embedding calls (consumption model). We can carve out embeddings from the slab if BrightCart prefers separate treatment — usually applies when embeddings volume is large.

2) Credit application: platform credits are applied to invoices in month-order until exhausted. The example $20k covers roughly ~16.6M tokens at 0.0012/token if you only use gen endpoints; with batching/quantization typical effective cost will be lower.

3) Overages and true-ups: if actual usage exceeds the committed baseline in a month, overage is billed at the next slab rate. We can add a 2-week buffer window for the first month after go-live for smoothing. 

If procurement wants a PO-ready single-line item, we can provide an itemization: PoC credit, estimated committed baseline, and discounted per-token unit prices.

-Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Evelyn/Markus — thanks for the notes. Summary and attachments sent: 1-page PoC SOW (DocuSign-ready), single-line PO language, and a short PoC SLA (response and uptime targets).

Responses to asks: 
- Credit refundability: we treat the PoC credit as refundable only against consumption billing (i.e., if you consume less than the credit and elect not to convert, we will refund remaining balance minus any third-party costs; for larger enterprise requests we can negotiate full refundability in the contract appendix).
- PO line: "Redwood Inference — BrightCart PoC credits (USD)" — amount: $20,000. Payment terms: net-30.
- SLA for PoC: 99.5% availability, tier-2 support response within 4 hours during business hours.

If that matches your procurement requirements we can send DocuSign tonight. As an incentive: if BrightCart signs a 6-month reserved baseline within 30 days of PoC completion we will: (a) increase the credit to $30k, (b) apply the extra 5% off list prices for the first billing quarter, and (c) provide a joint launch feature call to share performance tuning playbook.

Please see attached files and the HubSpot link for deal notes. Let me know if procurement needs any language tweaks.

Thanks,
Laura
